description: Milk substitution data for cheese-making recipes

cow.name: Cow Milk
cow.notes: Baseline milk for most cheese recipes. Larger fat globules may require homogenization.

goat.name: Goat Milk
goat.texture_notes: Soft, crumbly curds; creamy when fresh
goat.notes: Low alpha-s1 casein creates softer curds. Higher lipase gives distinctive tangy flavor. Naturally homogenized.

sheep.name: Sheep Milk
sheep.texture_notes: Firm curds, creamy mouthfeel, highest yield
sheep.notes: Highest fat and protein. Rich in calcium so no CaCl2 needed. Produces 2-3x more cheese per gallon than cow milk.

volume_conversions.description: Volume adjustments for equivalent cheese yield
notes: Sheep milk produces ~50-80% more cheese per volume
1 gallon sheep milk = ~1.6 gallons cow/goat milk for cheese yield
Adjust volumes based on desired final cheese quantity

rennet_adjustments.description: Rennet quantity adjustments when substituting milk types
notes: Sheep and goat milk require 30-40% less rennet than cow milk
Higher calcium in sheep milk accelerates coagulation
Lower alpha-s1 casein in goat milk affects curd structure
Species-specific rennets available (lamb rennet for sheep milk)

calcium_chloride_guidelines.description: CaCl2 addition guidelines by milk type and processing
notes: Sheep milk casein is naturally rich in calcium
Ultra-pasteurized/UHT milk destroys protein structure - unsuitable for cheese
Sheep milk should not exceed 104F (40C) for most cheeses
Lower temperatures produce moister, softer cheese

goat.notes: Fragile curds require delicate handling. Pronounced syneresis.

sheep.notes: Firm curds tolerate handling. Slow whey expulsion - allow extra draining time.

cow.notes: Most neutral flavor, highlights aging and cultures

goat.notes: Distinctive tang from capric/caprylic fatty acids

sheep.notes: Highest richness due to fat content. Famous cheeses: Roquefort, Pecorino, Manchego

substitution_warnings: Cheese texture will differ when substituting milk types
Some traditional cheeses are defined by their milk type (PDO/AOC)
Ultra-pasteurized milk cannot be used for cheese making

ingredient_adjustments.description: Which recipe ingredients need adjustment when substituting
notes: Starter cultures work the same across milk types
Salt ratios based on cheese weight, not milk volume
